scenario.name: Citizen Lab FORCEDENTRY, Google Project Zero & Apple CVE-2021-30860 — iOS JBIG2 Stream & MVT Shutdown/DataUsage Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a stately national art museum gallery with framed paintings on marble walls, velvet stanchion ropes, illuminated glass display pedestals, and thin security laser beams. Inside the hushed art museum hall, a thief studies how the velvet stanchions and glass pedestal sensors respond to routine curator maintenance checks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the velvet rope gallery entrance disguised as a regular visitor, then smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches. During closing inspection, the museum curator checks the gallery motion-sensor log and spots a brief laser shadow that never matched any scheduled restoration. In this scenario (T1203, Citizen Lab FORCEDENTRY, Google Project Zero & Apple CVE-2021-30860, iOS JBIG2 Stream & MVT Shutdown/DataUsage Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval, then coreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment, then dataUsage.sqlite. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval, then CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment, then DataUsage.sqlite, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1203 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1203 - Exploitation for Client Execution)
stages.description: Inside the hushed art museum hall, a thief studies how the velvet stanchions and glass pedestal sensors respond to routine curator maintenance checks. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the velvet rope gallery entrance disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the museum curator go about their routine. When a zero-click iMessage attachment (.gif wrapping a PDF/JBIG2 stream) arrives from Apple Push Notification service (APNs), IMTransferAgent automatically downloads the attachment from iCloud MMCS servers into ~/Library/SMS/Attachments/ without user interaction (logged in Linux Audit Event 101 with ProcessName=IMTransferAgent, AttachmentPath=~/Library/SMS/Attachments/9f/15/FA812B/IMG_0041.gif, HeaderMismatch=File extension .gif contains %PDF-1.3 header with /Filter /JBIG2Decode so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mvt-ios check-backup --iocs pegasus_forcedentry.stix2 /cases/ios_backup_decrypted/ (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1203 during "Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit"). Next, the follow-up artifact sqlite3 sms.db "SELECT rowid, filename, mime_type, total_bytes FROM attachment WHERE filename LIKE '%.gif';" runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 sms.db "SELECT rowid, filename, mime_type, total_bytes FROM attachment so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1203 during "Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/IMTransferServices.framework/IMTransferAgent / ⇠#1 ACK 101) from Node ① (#1 iMessage Attachment Delivery) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 DataUsage.sqlite & CrashReporter).

stages.title: Stage 2: CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment Integer Overflow (CVE-2021-30860) CrashReporter Trace
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1203 - Exploitation for Client Execution)
stages.description: Using a mirror-angle trick that satisfies the glass case laser beam, the thief lifts the cover and swaps a priceless artifact for a weight-matched replica. Here in Step 2 inside the art museum, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the permanent restoration wing. As CoreGraphics renders the masqueraded attachment outside the BlastDoor sandboxed image path, the JBIG2Stream::readTextRegionSeg parser processes over 70,000 segment commands using bitwise AND/OR/XOR/XNOR refinement operators, leaving diagnostic traces in CrashReporter and system logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 30860 with VulnerabilityId=CVE-2021-30860 , FORCEDENTRY CoreGraphics JBIG2 Integer Overflow, TargetProcess=IMTranscoderAgent / SpringBoard, ForensicArtifact=/private/var/mobile/Library/Logs/CrashReporter/IMTranscoderAgent-*.ips so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact mvt-ios check-fs --output /cases/mvt_out/ /cases/ios_filesystem_dump/ runs (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1203 during "CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment Integer Overflow , CVE-2021-30860 CrashReporter Trace"). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/IMTranscoding.framework/XPCServices/IMTranscoderAgent.xpc / ⇠#2 ACK 30860) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 IMTransferAgent & BlastDoor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 DataUsage.sqlite & CrashReporter).

stages.title: Stage 3: DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite Masqueraded Process Network Attribution
stages.subtitle: Command and Control (T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols)
stages.description: The glass pedestal seals back down without tripping the lobby bell, leaving visitors admiring a convincing decoy behind the velvet ropes. In this final step inside the art museum, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches until the gallery motion-sensor console catches the mismatch. Even after the staged files under /private/var/tmp/ are deleted (since Pegasus runs purely in memory and does not persist across reboots), iOS SQLite databases DataUsage.sqlite and netusage.sqlite permanently record cellular and Wi-Fi byte counts attributed to anomalous process names (such as RoleAccountd or Stagingd) with zero bundle ID (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with DatabaseArtifact=/private/var/wireless/Library/Databases/DataUsage.sqlite , ZPROCESS / ZLIVEUSAGE, AnomalousProcessName=RoleAccountd , ZPROCNAME with NULL ZBUNDLENAME, TemporalCorrelation=Spawned 7 seconds after IMTransferAgent attachment download so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). steps.simpleExplanation: Even after the staged files under /private/var/tmp/ are deleted (since Pegasus runs purely in memory and does not persist across reboots), iOS SQLite databases DataUsage.sqlite and netusage.sqlite permanently record cellular and Wi-Fi byte counts attributed to anomalous process names (such as RoleAccountd or Stagingd) with zero bundle ID (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with DatabaseArtifact=/private/var/wireless/Library/Databases/DataUsage.sqlite , ZPROCESS / ZLIVEUSAGE, AnomalousProcessName=RoleAccountd , ZPROCNAME with NULL ZBUNDLENAME, TemporalCorrelation=Spawned 7 seconds after IMTransferAgent attachment download so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIIN, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIOUT, datetime(ZPROCESS.ZFIRSTTIMESTAMP+978307200,'unixepoch') FROM ZLIVEUSAGE JOIN ZPROCESS ON ZLIVEUSAGE.ZHASPROCESS = ZPROCESS.Z_PK WHERE ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME IS NULL;" (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLI so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1071.001 during "DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite Masqueraded Process Network Attribution" under the database daemon's service account).
